content: Plan: Forecaster -> Uncertainty <-> Critic (revision loop) -> Critic risk -> Planner.
Goal: forecast demand 7 periods ahead for 36 series. Every sales-derived feature must be at least that old, otherwise the evaluation leaks the future.
Top demand drivers (permutation importance): roll_mean_28, price_rel, dow, item_code, temp_feat, is_event
Held-out validation WAPE: gbm 0.279, blend 0.277, seasonal_naive 0.437, ets 0.323; blend weight on the model chosen on the calibration window = 0.8.
Using 'gbm' (validation WAPE 0.279; 36% lower than seasonal naive).
Goal: 90% prediction intervals. Counts get noisier as demand grows, so residuals are scaled by sqrt(forecast+1) and calibrated per series with shrinkage to the global value.
Coverage on the held-out validation window is 90.3% (target 90%); bias -4.2%.

Errors on consecutive days are correlated, so multi-period demand is more uncertain than independent daily sigmas suggest: the standardised error of P-period sums has std 1.07 on validation. Planner sigma will be inflated by x1.07.
Reliability scores computed per series (1 - validation WAPE). Least reliable: S3_I05, S2_I05, S3_I12.

Three signals are checked for every series-period: (1) calendar events, (2) weather far outside the training climate for series that are weather-sensitive, in the direction that raises demand, (3) recent forecast errors that are worse than during validation. Each raises the risk multiplier.
Test window: 7.1% of series-periods have an event flag, 9.7% a weather flag, 16.3% an error-drift flag, 0.2% a price flag; mean risk multiplier 1.31.
Risk multipliers published to the Uncertainty agent (interval widening) and the Planner (safety stock).

base_stock policy: order-up-to = expected demand over 3 periods (lead time 2 + review 1) plus z=1.64 x forecast std (95% target). Five policies are compared on the same test window as a ladder: classical -> better forecast -> calibrated uncertainty -> Critic risk -> nowcast correction, so each agent's contribution can be separated.
gbm_static: fill rate 94.6%, stockout rate 8.8%, avg stock 14.1 units, total cost 8213.5.
agentic: fill rate 97.5%, stockout rate 4.3%, avg stock 20.1 units, total cost 4006.2.
Agentic policy fill rate 97.5% vs 91.1% for the classical policy; stockout rate 4.3% vs 12.0%.
